analysis.one_liner: Bajaj Finance is a large diversified NBFC that lends to consumers and small businesses across personal loans, consumer durables, SME/business loans, mortgages and gold loans, majority-owned by parent Bajaj Finserv.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (Oct 19, 2026): consolidated net profit rose 28.7% YoY to ₹6,367 crore, AUM grew 26% to ₹5,84,624 crore, and management raised FY27 growth guidance. The stock still fell about 3% afterwards because ₹1,047 crore of gold loans migrated into early-stress (Stage 2) on short-tenor schemes that the company has now discontinued, and analysts flagged margin pressure from rising funding costs. Separately, the board approved on Oct 1 a ₹17,500 crore capital raise (₹11,700 crore QIP plus ₹5,800 crore convertible warrants to parent Bajaj Finserv), still pending shareholder approval.
analysis.plain_terms: Bajaj Finance lends money to tens of millions of Indians and businesses and earns the spread between its borrowing cost and lending rate. Profit and loan growth both look strong this quarter, but the stock has barely beaten the Nifty over five years while its direct peer Shriram Finance has more than tripled - that gap is the real story here, not any single quarter. On top of that, the company is about to issue a large chunk of new shares, which dilutes existing holders' claim on future profit, and a normally reliable gold-loan product just showed its first real cracks.
analysis.quarters: NII grew 23-24% YoY to ₹13,335 crore and net total income rose 23% to ₹15,974 crore in the September 2026 quarter; PAT grew faster than revenue at 28.7%, helped by ROA rising to 4.6% (from 4.5%) and ROE to 20.6% annualised (from 19.1%) - this looks like genuine operating improvement, not an accounting shift, since no restatement or 'not comparable' language was flagged by the company. The one real blemish: ₹1,047 crore of gold loans slipped into Stage 2 on short-tenor schemes now withdrawn - a credit event in one product line, not a book-keeping artifact. GNPA improved to 1.06% (from 1.24% a year ago) and NNPA to 0.42% (from 0.60%) at the consolidated level, so asset quality is improving overall even as this one pocket showed stress.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 18.7% from its Aug 5, 2026 peak of ₹1,158.8 to ₹942.1, but that's within its 52-week range (₹796.65-₹1,158.8), not a breakdown to new lows - and the 2025 2:1 split and 2016 5:1 split are already reflected in these adjusted prices, so there's no corporate-action distortion to unwind here. The uncomfortable number is the longer-run comparison: 1-year return of -13.37% roughly tracks the Nifty's -12.37%, but over 3 years Bajaj Finance has returned 22.91% against the Nifty's 17.66% and peer Shriram Finance's 151.21%, and over 5 years it has returned 25.3% - almost exactly matching the Nifty's 25.24% - while Shriram Finance returned 224.05%. For a stock once considered a structural compounder, five years of Nifty-matching returns while a direct peer multiplied is the fact to sit with before looking at anything else.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E sits roughly in the 26-30x range (sources vary by date/basis) and price-to-book is about 4.68x, with ROE around 17.8% on a trailing basis (20.6% if you annualise the latest quarter). That is still a clear premium to peer Shriram Finance (~18.9x P/E) and to parent Bajaj Finserv (~25.9x). Why it is priced this way: the market is still paying for 26% AUM growth and improving ROE/ROA. Whether that premium is justified is a separate question - the pending QIP is expected to shave roughly 3% off near-term EPS growth, and a premium multiple on earnings that are about to be diluted is a weaker setup than the same multiple on undiluted earnings.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is broad-based rather than margin-engineered: AUM up 26% YoY, new loans booked up 11% to 13.45 million, and 4.42 million new customers added in the quarter, alongside margin improvement (ROE 19.1% to 20.6%). That combination of volume and margin both moving up is the more durable pattern this rulebook looks for. The watch item is that analysts (Nomura, among others) have flagged NIM headwinds as funding costs rise, which could turn this from a volume-and-margin story into a volume-only one if borrowing costs keep climbing.
analysis.health_read: Consolidated asset quality is improving (GNPA 1.06%, NNPA 0.42%, both down YoY), so the core book looks healthy. The real risk here is business risk concentrated in one product - the gold-loan Stage-2 slippage - rather than balance-sheet or liquidity risk; the ₹17,500 crore raise is capital to fund continued 26% growth, which is normal for a fast-growing NBFC, not a sign of distress. Not verified - check the cash flow statement on Screener to confirm how much of reported profit is converting to operating cash versus being re-lent out.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter group holds about 54.67% (parent Bajaj Finserv directly held 51.32% as of March 2026), with no pledge or encumbrance disclosed in the FY26 annual report - a clean, unencumbered promoter stake. FIIs hold 10.57% and DIIs about 16.40% (mutual funds 9.63% within that), with public holding around 6.62%. There is no marquee individual investor on the register in the data checked - this is an institutionally-held stock, and the pending warrant issue to Bajaj Finserv is specifically designed to let the promoter maintain its ~51% stake through the dilution from the QIP.
strengths: Consolidated PAT up 28.7% YoY to ₹6,367 crore in Q2 FY27
AUM crossed ₹5.85 lakh crore, up 26% YoY with ₹37,680 crore added in the quarter
GNPA improved to 1.06% (from 1.24% YoY) and NNPA to 0.42% (from 0.60% YoY)
ROE improved to 20.6% annualised and ROA to 4.6%, both up from the year-ago quarter
watchpoints: ₹1,047 crore of gold loans moved into Stage 2 this quarter; the short-tenor scheme behind it has been discontinued
₹17,500 crore capital raise (₹11,700cr QIP + ₹5,800cr warrants to Bajaj Finserv) awaiting shareholder approval, estimated to dampen near-term EPS growth by ~3%
Stock down 18.7% from its Aug 2026 peak with brokerages flagging NIM pressure from rising funding costs
5-year and 3-year returns badly trail peer Shriram Finance (25.3% and 22.91% vs 224.05% and 151.21%) despite similar or better headline growth
analysis.one_thing: Whether gold-loan Stage-2 slippage stabilizes and the QIP completes without further EPS drag in the Q3 FY27 results will show whether the current growth premium over peers is still earned.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 PAT, NII, AUM and asset-quality figures were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Upstox, Equitybulls, Kalkine, scanx) and are consistent. P/E estimates varied by source (26.3x to 30.15x depending on date/basis) - a range is given rather than a single number. ROE is reported two ways by different sources (17.8% trailing vs 20.6% quarter-annualised) and both are included rather than averaged. Precise cash-flow-to-profit conversion and book value per share could not be verified - check Screener directly.
